8-3A-1: - Zoning Districts and Purposes Established
","ShouldShowMiniToc":false,"Id":"TIT8UNDECO_CH3ZODIST_ARTADIES_8-3A-1ZODIPUES","Title":"8-3A-1: - Zoning Districts and Purposes Established","Content":"
\n

\n The following zoning districts are hereby established. For the interpretation of this\n title, the zoning districts have been formulated to realize the general purposes as\n set forth in this title. In addition, the specific purpose of each zoning district\n shall be as follows:\n

\n

\n (A) AGRICULTURAL DISTRICT: To provide for agricultural use with parcels that are 5\n acres or larger in size. May include active agriculture, viticulture, equestrian,\n and residential. Uses include native open space and active farmland. The agricultural\n land use is not amenity based (sewer, water, schools) and will usually be located\n away from goods and services. These areas encourage the keeping and raising of crops\n and/or animals and do not necessarily include manicured yards, sidewalks, bike paths,\n streetlights or planned park and recreation facilities. Density may be limited due\n to the limited availability of infrastructure. Wells and septic systems should be\n permitted for lots in this land use designation if approved by the applicable Health\n Department. Easements of at least 20-feet in width shall be provided where determined\n necessary for the future extension of water and sewer mains. Modified street sections\n and a reduction in light pollution (by reducing or eliminating lighting standards)\n may be offered for a more rural feel. Private streets may be permitted in this district\n for access to newly subdivided or split property. This district does allow for some\n commercial uses as specified in 8-3A-3.\n

\n

\n (RR) RURAL-RESIDENTIAL DISTRICT: To provide for rural single-family residential use\n adjacent to agricultural uses, adjacent to other Rural Residential type uses, and\n adjacent to BLM land areas. Parcels are to be two acres minimum. It is the intent\n of this land use designation to help to preserve Star's rural feel. Huge manicured\n \"Rural Residential\" lots are discouraged and therefore manicured home site areas on\n these properties should not exceed 1/2 acre. Uses may include active agriculture,\n viticulture, equestrian, and residential. Uses include native open space and small-scale\n active farmland. The Rural Residential land use is not amenity based (sewer, water,\n schools) and will usually be located away from goods and services. These areas encourage\n the keeping and raising of small-scale crops and/or animals and do not necessarily\n include manicured yards, sidewalks, bike paths, streetlights or planned park and recreation\n facilities. Density may be further limited due to the limited availability of infrastructure.\n Modified street sections and a reduction in light pollution (by reducing or eliminating\n lighting standards) may be offered for a more rural feel. Private streets may be permitted\n in this district for access to newly subdivided or split property. This land use designation\n is to be located such that it does not block extension of urban services at reasonable\n costs. Wells and septic systems should be permitted for lots in this land use designation\n if approved by the applicable Health Department. Easements of at least 20-feet in\n width shall be provided where determined necessary for the future extension of water\n and sewer mains. This district does allow for some commercial uses as specified in\n 8-3A-3.\n

\n

\n (R) RESIDENTIAL DISTRICT: To provide regulations and districts for various residential\n neighborhoods. Gross density in a Residential (R) district shall be determined according\n to the numeral following the R. The numeral designates the maximum number of dwelling\n units per acre. In zoning designations of R-1, R-2, R-3, R-4 and R-5, housing shall\n be single family detached unless approved with a PUD or development agreement. Connection\n to municipal water and sewer facilities are required for all subdivision and lot split\n applications submitted after the effective date hereof in all districts exceeding\n one dwelling unit per acre. Wells and septic systems may be permitted for larger lots\n in this land use designation that are not adjacent to municipal services, as determined\n by the Sewer District, and if approved by the applicable Health Department. Private\n streets may be approved in this district for access to newly subdivided or split property.\n This district does allow for some non-residential uses as specified in 8-3A-3.\n

\n

\n (RC) RIVERFRONT CENTER: To provide for a mixture of uses which may, at the sole discretion\n of the Council, include office, small-scale retail, restaurants, offices, entertainment,\n and high-density residential within the comprehensive plan area designated as Riverfront\n Center. The Riverfront Center is planned to be a vibrant mixed-use center for the\n community that builds off River access and connection north to Main Street, the Riverwalk\n Park, and the River House. High density housing is encouraged on the upper floors\n of buildings and at the fringes of the land use designation. The focus of the Riverfront\n Center is a large-scale community civic space and gathering area at the Boise River\n edge. Development within this zone is to proceed through the PUD process unless a\n development agreement has already been executed for the particular property. This\n zone may allow the development community to be more innovative in design and placement\n of structures subject to Council review and approval. Rezoning within this land use\n designation is to be strictly monitored by the city to assure that the Riverfront\n Center is not being used simply to justify high density residential use. High-density\n residential uses should be part of the Riverfront Center though may not exceed thirty\n percent (30%) of the overall size of the development.\n

\n

\n (CBD) CENTRAL BUSINESS DISTRICT: To provide for commercial, retail, civic, office,\n and entertainment uses. Residential uses, including higher densities may be allowed\n on the upper floors of multiple use buildings and may also be allowed at the fringes\n of the land use designation shown on the comprehensive plan. Live/work designed development\n is also encouraged in this district. Developments in this district are to place an\n emphasis on pedestrian and bicycle access and compatibility. Special emphasis shall\n be placed on development in the central downtown area to encourage and create a vibrant,\n walkable downtown community that incorporates the Boise River as an active amenity.\n

\n

\n (C-1) NEIGHBORHOOD COMMERCIAL DISTRICT: To provide for the establishment of convenience\n business uses which tend to meet the daily needs of the residents of an immediate\n neighborhood while establishing development standards that prevent adverse effects\n on residential uses adjoining a C-1 district. Such districts are typically appropriate\n for small shopping clusters or integrated shopping centers located within residential\n neighborhoods, where compatible.\n

\n

\n (C-2) GENERAL COMMERCIAL DISTRICT: To provide for the establishment of areas for commercial\n uses allowed in other commercial zones and commercial uses which are more intensive\n than those permitted in other commercial zones, and typically located adjacent to\n arterial roadways and not immediately adjacent to residential, including the establishment\n of areas for travel related services such as hotels, motels, service stations, drive-in\n restaurants, offices, limited warehousing, commercial services and retail sales.\n

\n

\n (LO) LIMITED OFFICE DISTRICT: To provide for the establishment of groupings of professional,\n research, executive, administrative, accounting, clerical, limited commercial and\n similar uses. Development shall not be traffic intensive and research facilities shall\n not involve heavy testing operations of any kind. The L-O district is designed to\n act as a buffer between other more intense nonresidential uses and residential uses\n and is thus a transitional use.\n

\n

\n (LI) LIGHT INDUSTRIAL DISTRICT: To provide for manufacturing, warehousing, mini-storage\n and open storage, multi-tenant industrial park, contractors yards, and similar uses.\n Limited office and commercial uses may be permitted as ancillary uses. All development\n within this land use shall be free of hazardous or objectionable elements such as\n excessive noise, odor, dust, smoke, or glare.\n

\n

\n (PS) PUBLIC/SEMIPUBLIC: To provide for the development of such uses as golf courses,\n parks, recreation facilities, greenways, schools, cemeteries, and public service facilities\n such as government offices and utilities. All development within this land use is\n encouraged to be designed to accommodate the different needs, interests, and age levels\n of residents in matters concerning both recreation and civil activities.\n

\n

\n (MU) MIXED USE DISTRICT: To provide for a mixture of uses which may, at the sole discretion\n of the Council, include office, commercial, and/or residential depending upon the\n specific comprehensive plan area designated as Mixed Use. Development within this\n zone is to proceed through the PUD process unless a development agreement has already\n been executed for the particular property. Identifying areas for mixed-use development\n has two objectives. The first objective is to give the city a better tool to manage\n the type of developments through the planned unit development and/or the Development\n Agreement process. The second objective is that this zone may allow the development\n community to be more innovative in design and placement of structures subject to Council\n review and approval. Rezoning within this land use designation is to be strictly monitored\n by the city to assure that the Mixed-Use areas are not being used simply to justify\n high density residential use. Residential uses may be part of an overall mixed-use\n development that includes a non-residential component and may not exceed 30% of the\n overall size of the development.\n

\n

\n (PUD) PLANNED UNIT DEVELOPMENT: This designation, following any zoning designation\n noted on the official zoning map of the city (i.e., R-4-PUD), indicates that the development\n was approved by the city as a planned unit development, with specific allowances and\n design approved by Council.\n

\n

\n (DA) DEVELOPMENT AGREEMENT: This designation, following any zoning designation noted\n on the official zoning map of the city (i.e., C-2-DA), indicates that the zoning was\n approved by the city with a development agreement, with specific conditions of zoning.\n

\n

\n (Ord. 303, 2-11-2020; amd. Ord. 310, 7-21-2020; Repealed & Replaced by Ord. 370-2022 on 7/19/2022; Amended by Ord. 404-2024 on 6/18/2024)\n
